title: Trace Contract Verifier and Sink Onboarding
creator: Micah Soto
description: Create a lightweight contract verification and onboarding harness to validate that new or updated tracing backend sinks (Jaeger-compatible vendors, Tempo, and OTLP ingestion endpoints) accept Redwood-generated trace envelopes and tags without loss or transformation that would break our latency/error dashboards or span stitching. The tool should be usable by platform engineers to smoke-test vendor endpoints and by the onboarding flow for Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: A small probe service that can emit synthetic traces with configurable attributes (traceid formats, sampled flags, typical attribute sets used by Redwood) is implemented and containerized.
Probe validates vendor responses: spans received, traceid preserved/stitchable, service/name/tag schema preserved, and no unwarranted tag redaction observed.
A contract test harness runs against Jaeger/Tempo/OTLP endpoints and reports pass/fail per rule with a human-readable report (HTML or Markdown) and machine-readable JSON output.
Integrate probe runs into onboarding CI pipeline and a one-click run from Console (developer/ops path) for Private deployments.
Documentation describing test cases, failure modes, and remediation steps live in Confluence and linked from onboarding flow.
Two vendor endpoints (one Jaeger-compatible hosted vendor, one Tempo-compatible managed service) successfully pass the default test set in staging.
implementation_notes: Write probe in Go to reuse existing tracing SDKs and our trace serializer utilities.
Probe will support adjustable sampling, chunked/batch sends, and both HTTP thrift and OTLP/gRPC transports to cover common vendor setups.

Contract rules will include: traceid format normalization checks, parent-child relationship integrity, span duration sanity checks, attribute presence/absence rules, and latency histogram sanity for synthetic requests.
Store expected/observed diffs in S3 for postmortem and for future regression tests.
Expose a /report endpoint on the probe that returns JSON summary to be consumed by the onboarding CI job.
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Spike complete. Implemented PoC sender using OTLP gRPC and verified ingestion into local Tempo dev cluster.
2025-11-06: Defined initial contract rules (traceid preservation, attribute whitelist, span count) after consulting with Console and Runtime owners.
2025-11-09: Built container image and ran probe against vendor-qa environment; observed tag key normalization issue on vendor B (investigating transformation behavior).
2025-11-12: Added parent-child integrity check and started wiring CI job in onboarding pipeline (PR open).
review_feedback: PM (Rina Patel): Prefer to include an explicit UX flow in Console for ops to trigger onboarding test runs; added as follow-up story if scope exceeds estimate.
Security (Jonas Müller): Ensure probe creds are ephemeral and rotated for vendor onboarding; suggested short-lived tokens and audit logging — marked as dependency for onboarding pipeline.
Design (Luisa Romero): Suggested report should surface a simple pass/fail badge plus an expandable diff for engineers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Some vendors rewrite attributes leading to false negatives. Mitigation: classify tests as WARN vs FAIL and provide remediation guidance rather than blocking onboarding by default.
Risk: Probe could overload vendor endpoints in aggressive mode. Mitigation: default to low-rate synthetic tests and require operator confirmation for stress tests.
Risk: Private deployments may have network constraints. Mitigation: provide offline mode to capture and re-play traces to vendor endpoints from within customer VPC.
next_steps: Finish PR feedback (unit tests and CI glue) — target 2025-11-14.
Run full contract suite against vendor QA endpoints and record failures for follow-up (2025-11-16).
Create Console integration story (PM follow-up) to expose a run button and report viewer — scope to be estimated.
notes: This ticket focuses on the verification tooling and CI integration. Any vendor-specific adapters discovered during testing should become separate follow-up tasks (tagged vendor-<name>-adapter).
Keep test rules extensible: rules should be declarative YAML to allow adding new checks without code changes.
